items.why: The fear gauge rose nearly 5 percent as stocks opened lower, with oil topping $100 and Middle East tensions rattling the tape, per CNBC and the WSJ.
Crude rallied to a five-month high near $102 as escalating Iran tensions drove oil prices higher, per the WSJ and Investopedia.
Chip stocks steadied and memory names rebounded even as the broader tape sagged, lifting AMD into the green, per MarketWatch and Investopedia.
The Dow opened lower and shed about 550 points as rising oil prices and Middle East tensions weighed on stocks, per the WSJ and Investopedia.

market_note: Risk-off open: indexes lower, Dow down about 550, VIX up nearly 5 percent, gold softer, oil near a five-month high.
summary: Stocks opened lower Friday as oil pushed past $100 on escalating Iran tensions, pulling the Dow and S&P down. Tech stayed choppy after this week's sharp selloff, with chip names steadying only slightly.
